fact: The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications' National Data Governance Policy lists the National Digital Strategy (2025-2029) among the policy instruments Liberia 'has adopted', with a main focus on digital governance and cybersecurity and a Data Marketplace for economic growth; it names no adopting act or date, so the date used is the policy's own (March 2026).

The National Data Governance Policy (March 2026) states that the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications' responsibilities include implementation of the National Digital Strategy (2025-2029) and that it developed the strategy; it names no budget line for the strategy.

The strategy text, titled 'Whole of Government' National Digital Strategy (2025-2029) and held on the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications website, states a five-year period of 2025-2029 for its cost estimates and roadmap; no event date is given, so the date used is the document's published date (3 February 2026), which falls inside that period.

Chapter 6 gives financial estimates: US$151.813 million for initiatives funded from government, multilateral donor and other sources over 2025-2029 (US$90.200 million capital plus US$61.613 million operating), and a separate US$776.250 million for about 1,500 cell towers to be funded through public-private partnership; Chapter 7 sets an implementation roadmap with timelines; the estimate carries no date of its own, so the published date is used.

The strategy states that its intervention areas came from stakeholder working sessions on 3 and 4 December 2024 and a validation workshop on 11 December 2024, with further feedback through January 2025; it names no adopting act.

The strategy's current-state review says there is no standalone central institution focused solely on coordinating ICT implementation across the Government of Liberia, and it recommends establishing a Liberia Digital Transformation Agency by legislation or executive order, with a National Digital Transformation Working Group proposed by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications in the interim; the strategy is undated on this point, so the published date is used.

The strategy's cost chapter says its estimates are to be funded from government sources, multilateral donors and other agencies, and lists availability of financial resources as a critical success factor; it names no budget line or allocation for the strategy; the published date is used.
The document is the strategy's own text, published on the ministry's site (mopt.gov.lr).

The Digital Liberia Week event book records that its National Coordination Session, held during 28-30 October 2025, marked the official launch of Liberia's National Digital Strategy (2025-2029); the launch is by event participants and ministry officials, with no head of state or adopting act named, and the session day is not given.

The same session activated the Digital Transformation Working Group, which the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications' Assistant Minister for Technical Services said will coordinate Liberia's digital activities on infrastructure, skills, governance, the digital economy and cybersecurity; the record names no act establishing it and no budget line.
